Cal Poly Pomona’s Electrical & Computer Engineering department offers ABET-accredited Bachelor of Science degrees in Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering, alongside a Master of Science in Electrical Engineering. With a curriculum grounded in the “learn by doing” philosophy, students engage in extensive hands-on laboratories-covering circuits, embedded systems, signal processing, and power electronics-alongside rigorous theoretical instruction. Faculty with industry and research expertise guide students in real-world applications, fostering a learning culture rooted in practical problem-solving, innovation, and ethical professionalism. Students build their skills through multidisciplinary senior capstone projects, access to state-of-the-art labs, and involvement in applied research within the Master of Science in Electrical Engineering program. Co-curricular opportunities through Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), Eta Kappa Nu honor society, and other student organizations provide professional development, networking, and technical workshops. With strong advising, career support, and industry partnerships, Electrical and Computer Engineering graduates emerge as proficient professionals ready to contribute to sectors such as telecommunications, power systems, computing, cybersecurity, robotics, and beyond. courses.title: Electrical Circuit Analysis I
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamental laws of electric circuits, applications to circuit analysis, matrix methods. An introduction to circuit analysis in the time domain using differential equations with computer tools. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and MAT 1140 or MAT 114.

courses.title: Electrical Circuit Analysis I Laboratory
courses.description: Selected laboratory experiments emphasizing the fundamental laws of electric circuits, applications to circuit analysis, matrix methods; supporting the topics covered in ECE 1101. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and MAT 1140 or MAT 114. Pre or Corequisite(s): ECE 1101 .

courses.title: C For Engineers
courses.description: Computer programming for ECE. Problem-oriented computer language applications to electrical networks.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and MAT 1140 or MAT 114.

courses.title: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Fundamental topics for Computer Engineering, including mathematical logic, sets and relations, basic counting rules, permutations and combinations, probability, matrices, functions and recursions, graphs and trees.
courses.prerequisites: ECE major. Pre or Corequisite(s): MAT 1140 .

courses.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Electrical Circuit Analysis II
courses.description: RLC circuit analysis in the time domain using differential equations, AC phasor analysis, AC steady state power, complex circuit functions, Laplace transform methods, convolution, and analog filter design. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 109 or ECE 1101 ; MAT 224 or MAT 2240 ; PHY 133 or PHY 1520 ; and ECE 109L or ECE 1101L .

courses.title: Electrical Circuit Analysis II Laboratory
courses.description: Selected laboratory exercises in electrical circuits such as RLC circuit analysis in the time domain, AC phasor analysis, AC steady state power, convolution, Laplace transform methods, and active filter design. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 1101L , ECE 109L, ECE 207L, ECE 299L, or ECE 2990L . Pre or Corequisite(s): ECE 2101 or ECE 209.

courses.title: Introduction to Microelectronics Circuits
courses.description: Behavior of semiconductor devices including diodes and MOSFETS: modes of operation and IV characteristics. Diode circuit analysis. Amplifier biasing. Application of large signal models to single stage amplifiers to determine voltage transfer curves. Introduction to CMOS digital logic gates including latches. Transient analysis of CMOS logic gates. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; CHM 1210 or CHM 1150 ; and C- or better in ECE 1101 . Pre or Corequisite(s): ECE 2300 .

courses.title: Introduction to Microelectronics Circuits Laboratory
courses.description: Design, construction and characterization of microelectronic diode and transistor circuits with an emphasis on large signal performance. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 1101L , ECE 109L, ECE 299L, or ECE 2990L; and C- or better in ECE 2200 , ECE 220, or ECE 299.

courses.title: Digital Logic Design
courses.description: Analysis and design of both combinational and sequential circuits. Use of HDL to synthesize digital logic circuits.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; C- or better in ECE 1310 or ECE 114 ; C- or better in ECE 1101 , ECE 109, or ECE 299; and C- or better in ECE 109L, ECE 1101L , or ECE 299L.

courses.title: Digital Logic Design Laboratory
courses.description: Design, implementation and testing of combinational and sequential circuits. 3 hours of laboratory.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 1310 or ECE 114; ECE 1101 , ECE 109, ECE 299, or ECE 2990 ; and ECE 1101L , ECE 109L, or ECE 299L. Pre or Corequisite(s): ECE 2300 .

courses.title: Object Oriented Programming
courses.description: Class encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, object storage management, and exception handling. Program debugging, software reuse and object-oriented programming.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, and C- or better in ECE 1310 or ECE 114.

courses.title: Special Topics for Lower Division Students
courses.description: Group study of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Special Topics for Lower Division Students Activity
courses.description: Group study of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.description: Group study of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Signals and Systems
courses.description: Basic principles of both continuous-time and discrete-time signals and systems. Frequency domain analysis of continuous-time signals, Fourier series and Fourier Transform. Time and frequency domain analysis of discrete-time signals and systems, sampling, z-transform, discrete Fourier series and transform. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 2101 or ECE 209.

courses.title: Signals and Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Selected experiments and simulations of continuous-time and discrete-time signals and systems.
courses.prerequisites: ECE major, ECE 2101 or ECE 209, and ECE 2101L or ECE 209L Pre or Corequisite(s): ECE 3101 or ECE 306.

courses.title: Microelectronic Devices and Circuits
courses.description: An overview of the basic properties of semiconductors. Physical structure and basic device modeling of p-n junctions, MOS capacitors and MOSFETs. Two port small-signal amplifiers and their realization using single stage and multistage building blocks. Frequency response of single and multi-stage amplifiers. Introduction to differential amplifiers. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; C- or better in ECE 2101 or ECE 209; and C- or better in ECE 2200 , ECE 220, or ECE 299.

courses.title: Analog Microelectronics Laboratory
courses.description: Design, construction and characterization of microelectronic circuits with an emphasis on analog signal conditioning. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 3200 or ECE 320; and ECE 2200L , ECE 220L, or ECE 299L.

courses.title: Instrumentation Systems
courses.description: Components of Instrumentation Systems. Typical power supplies and signal conditioners. A/D and D/A converters. Sensors for various parameters. Error analysis, readouts, recorders and actuators, piping and instrumentation diagrams (PandID).
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 2200 , ECE 220, or ECE 299; and PHY 1520 or PHY 133.

courses.title: Instrumentation Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Instrumentation system assignments based upon work of ECE 3201. Verification of design solutions.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 2200 , ECE 220, or ECE 299; and PHY 1520 or PHY 133. Pre or Corequisite(s): ECE 3201 .

courses.title: Electromagnetic Fields
courses.description: Maxwell’s equations and electromagnetic concepts. Introduction to static and time varying fields; plane waves, boundary conditions, and transmission line equations. Applications to analog and digital circuits.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; MAT 2140 , MAT 2140C, or MAT 215; MAT 2240 or MAT 224; PHY 1520 or PHY 133; and C- or better in ECE 2200 , ECE 220, or ECE 299.

courses.title: Digital Circuit Design Using Verilog
courses.description: Design of combinational circuits, finite state machines, digital systems with HDL. Implementation with FPGAs. Corequisite(s): ECE 3300L .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; C- or better in ECE 2300 or ECE 204; and C- or better in ECE 2300L or ECE 204L.

courses.title: Digital Circuit Design Using Verilog Laboratory
courses.description: Design and Simulation of digital systems using Verilog. Implementation of digital systems with FPGAs. Corequisite(s): ECE 3300 .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 2300 or ECE 204; and ECE 2300L or ECE 204L.

courses.title: Introduction to Microcontrollers
courses.description: Microcontroller programming, applications, and interfacing. Corequisite(s): ECE 3301L .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; C- or better in ECE 2300 or ECE 204; and C- or better in ECE 2300L or ECE 204L.

courses.title: Introduction to Microcontrollers Laboratory
courses.description: Microcontroller applications and interfacing. 3 hours of laboratory. Corequisite(s): ECE 3301 .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 2300 and ECE 2300L or ECE 204 and ECE 204L.

courses.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
courses.description: Implementation of data structures and algorithms using an object oriented programming language such as C++, C#, Java etc. Utilization of data structures such as stacks, linked lists, trees and graphs in solving engineering problems. Learning algorithms used in data mining, information retrieval etc. Use of advanced programming language construct such as C++ standard template library (STL) in code development.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and C- or better in ECE 2310 or ECE 256, and ECE 1320 .

courses.title: Control Systems Engineering
courses.description: System modeling and performance specifications of dynamic systems. Design and analysis of linear time invariant feedback control systems via root locus and frequency response compensation techniques.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, ECE 2101 or ECE 209, and MAT 2240 or MAT 224.

courses.title: Control Systems Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Control system design assignments based upon the coursework of ECE 3709 involving basic LabView programming skills.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major. Pre or Corequisite(s): ECE 3709 .

courses.title: Probability, Statistics, and Random Processes for Electrical and Computer Engineers
courses.description: Concepts of Probability, Statistics, Random variables, and Random processes. Basic estimation, minimum mean square error estimation, linear regression, analysis of random signals through linear time invariant systems
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; MAT 2140 , MAT 2140C, or MAT 215; and ECE 3101 or ECE 306.

courses.title: Introduction to Power Engineering
courses.description: Basic principles of power engineering with an emphasis on magnetics, transformers, and rotating AC and DC machines. Magnetic material characteristics and steady-state operational circuit models, as they apply to transformers and electrical machines. Power generation with synchronous and doubly-excited induction machines. Per-unit computations in power systems.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 2101 or ECE 209.

courses.title: Power Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Selected experiments in power engineering including 3-phase circuits, magnetics (inductors), transformers, AC and DC generators and motors, with the utilization of digital watt-meters, clamp-on ammeters, and dynamometers.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, and ECE 3810 or ECE 310.

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Professional Engineering Practice
courses.description: Preparation for the professional practice of engineering: career planning, resumes and interviewing, ethics, licensure, personal and organizational skills.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; junior or senior standing; and completion of all 1000 & 2000 level courses.

courses.title: CMOS Analog Circuits
courses.description: Analysis and design of analog circuits implemented using CMOS integrated circuit technology.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3200 or ECE 320.

courses.title: CMOS Analog Circuits Laboratory
courses.description: Analysis and design of analog circuits implemented using CMOS integrated circuit technology. Corequisite(s): ECE 4200 .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 4200 or ECE 407.

courses.title: Advanced Analog Circuit Design
courses.description: Analog circuit design with an emphasis on frequency response, stability, and the use of feedback. Topics include linear and nonlinear operational amplifier circuits, frequency response and compensation, stability and oscillation, power amplifier stages, data converters and phased-locked loops.
courses.prerequisites: ECE major; and ECE 3200 or ECE 320.

courses.title: Advanced Analog Circuit Design Laboratory
courses.description: Design, construction and characterization of analog circuits with an emphasis on frequency response, stability, and the use of feedback. Topics include linear and nonlinear operational amplifier circuits, frequency response and compensation, stability and oscillation, power amplifier stages, data converters and phased-locked loops.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3200 or ECE 320. Pre or Corequisite(s): ECE 4201 .

courses.title: VLSI (Very Large Scale Integrated) Circuit Design
courses.description: Integrated circuit chip design in silicon CMOS technology. Computer aided physical layout design and simulation of digital integrated circuits-combinational logic and sequential logic circuits. CMOS Fabrication. Optimizing speed, area, power
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3200 or ( ECE 2200 , ECE 220, or ECE 299; ECE 3300 or ECE 205); and PHY 1520 or PHY 133.

courses.title: VLSI (Very Large Scale Integrated) Circuit Design Laboratory
courses.description: Chip design laboratory. Computer aided physical layout design, simulation and verification of integrated circuits.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major. Pre or Corequisite(s): ECE 4203 or ECE 423.

courses.title: Image Sensors
courses.description: Principles of Photodetection. Image sensor and digital camera overview. CCD and CMOS image sensor: basic operation, pixel functionality, readout modes, readout signal chain, building blocks and architectures. Image sensor performance metics, non idealities and noise. Basic image processing algorithms. Advanced image sensor topics.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major and ECE 2200 . Pre or Corequisite(s): ECE 3715 .

courses.title: Fields and Waves in RF Electronics
courses.description: Electrodynamics, wave equations, and reflection and scattering of waves. Radio frequency applications of transmission line techniques, and Impedance matching. S-parameter design techniques, couplers, hybrids, and filters. Experiments on Impedance matching, RF circuits, antennas, and S-parameter measurements using Network Analyzers.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3250 or ECE 302.

courses.title: RF Design
courses.description: Principles of R.F. design of transmitters and receivers utilizing solid state electronic devices and integrated circuits. RF design techniques including S-parameters. Design of amplifiers, oscillator, mixers and detectors.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3250 or ECE 302.

courses.title: Integrated Circuit Design for Wireless Systems
courses.description: Introduction to various receiver and transmitter architectures with fundamental radio frequency (RF) concepts. The detailed analysis and designs of a power amplifier, a low-noise amplifier, and a mixer. Translation of wireless system specification to architectures and building blocks compatible with integrated circuit technology.

courses.title: Introduction to Photonics
courses.description: The nature of light. Simple geometric optics. Thermal and atomic-line light sources. Modulation of light. Nonlinear optics and parametric oscillation. Luminescence. Display devices. Lasers and laser light. Photodetectors. Common optical instruments. Optical waveguides
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 3250 or ECE 302; and ECE 3200 or ECE 320.

courses.title: Computer Architecture
courses.description: RISC architecture instruction sets, design of single cycle and pipelined RISC CPUs, performance evaluation, memory hierarchy and cache organization
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 3301 or ECE 341; ECE 3301L or ECE 341L; ECE 3300 or ECE 205; and ECE 3300L or ECE 205L.

courses.title: Cryptographic Algorithms on Reconfigurable Hardware
courses.description: Introduction to the cryptographic algorithms on reconfigurable hardware. The course covers cryptographic algorithms, solutions, and corresponding architectures for obtaining state-of-the-art finite field arithmetic realizations. The course covers three cryptographic building blocks and their implementation on reconfigurable logic devices: hash functions, symmetric block cipher and public key cryptosystems in the form of elliptic curve cryptography.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, ECE 3300 , and ECE 3300L .

courses.title: TCP / IP Internetworking
courses.description: Principles, Protocols, Architecture, Coding, and Performance Analyses of Transmission Control Protocol and Internet Protocol Suite. Also, related IEEE 802.11 Wireless standards. Corequisite(s): ECE 4303L .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 2310 or ECE 256; ECE 3301 or ECE 341; ECE 3301L or ECE 341L; ECE 3300 or ECE 205; and ECE 3300L or ECE 205L.

courses.title: TCP / IP Internetworking Laboratory
courses.description: Principles, Protocols, Architecture, Coding, and Performance Analyses of Transmission Control Protocol and Internet Protocol Suite. Also, related IEEE 802.11 Wireless standards. Corequisite(s): ECE 4303 .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 2310 or ECE 256; ECE 3301 or ECE 341; ECE 3301L or ECE 341L; ECE 3300 or ECE 205; and ECE 3300L or ECE 205L.

courses.title: Discrete System Design Using VHDL
courses.description: Design of discrete systems using VHDL for FPGA implementation. Corequisite(s): ECE 4304L .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 3101 or ECE 306; and ECE 3300 or ECE 205.

courses.title: Discrete System Design Using VHDL Laboratory
courses.description: Design of discrete systems using VHDL for FPGA implementation. Corequisite(s): ECE 4304 .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 3101 or ECE 306; ECE 3300 or ECE 205; and ECE 3300L or ECE 205L.

courses.title: Advanced Digital Design Using Verilog HDL
courses.description: Design, develop, synthesis, test, validation &verification digital systems using Verilog HDL and FPGA. Corequisite(s): ECE 4305L .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 2310 or ECE 256; ECE 3301 or ECE 341; ECE 3301L or ECE 341L, ECE 3300 or ECE 205; and ECE 3300L or ECE 205L.

courses.title: Advanced Digital Design Using Verilog HDL Laboratory
courses.description: Design, develop, synthesis, test, validation &verification digital systems using Verilog HDL and FPGA.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 2310 or ECE 256; ECE 3301 or ECE 341; and ECE 3301L or ECE 341L. Pre or Corequisite(s): ECE 4305 .

courses.title: Fundamentals of Cybersecurity
courses.description: An introduction to security concepts in computer networks, applications, mobile, access control and cryptography.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major and ECE 3310 .

courses.title: Operating Systems for Embedded Applications
courses.description: Operating system concepts including memory, device and file management techniques and design of a real time operating system for embedded controllers.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, and C- or better in ECE 3310 or ECE 304.

courses.title: Network Forensics
courses.description: Basic TCP/IP protocol concepts. Network analysis tools such as Wireshark. Packet Analysis. Statistical Flow Analysis. Network Intrusion Detection, Prevention, and Analysis. Network Devices and Protocols.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 2310 or ECE 256.

courses.title: Intelligence Systems for Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamental concepts of intelligence systems including search algorithms, machine learning, fuzzy logic, neural network, natural language processing, and AI programming.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 3310 or ECE 304; and ECE 3715 or ECE 315.

courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.description: Software requirements and specification, project management, modeling using UML, Petri-net and regular expression modeling, Software testing, Software metrics and measures, Risk and configuration management.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3310 or ECE 304.

courses.title: Application Development Using JAVA
courses.description: Essential object-oriented programming concepts: Encapsulation, Inheritance and Polymorphism, GUI Development, Multimedia Applications, Multi-tasking, Network Programming Using Internet.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 2310 or ECE 256.

courses.title: Microprocessor-based System Design
courses.description: Analysis and design of Computer Engineering Systems, including microprocessors. Assembly language programming. Microcomputer design and applications at the systems level. Corequisite(s): ECE 4320L .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 3301 or ECE 341; and ECE 3301L or ECE 341L.

courses.title: Microprocessor-based System Design Laboratory
courses.description: Design and build typical microprocessor-based applications from chip level. 1 three-hour laboratory. Corequisite(s): ECE 4320 .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 3301 or ECE 341; and ECE 3301L or ECE 341L.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence for Cyber Security
courses.description: In-depth exploration of the intersection between artificial intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity. Explore fundamental concepts of AI and machine learning techniques, and how they are applied to various aspects of cybersecurity, including threat detection, intrusion detection and prevention, malware analysis, and security analytics. Through hands-on exercises and real-world case studies, develop practical skills in using AI tools and techniques to address cybersecurity challenges.
courses.prerequisites: ECE major and ECE 3715 .

courses.title: Mobile Autonomous Robots
courses.description: Introduction to the basic principles of robotics, including kinematics, robot sensor and motor, actuators, robot motion planning, control algorithms, localization, Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM), and applications like Robot Operating System (ROS), service robots, and robot arms programmed with ROS.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, ECE 3301 , and ECE 3301L .

courses.title: Robotics
courses.description: Introduction to robotics. Kinematics, position analysis, Denavit-Hartenberg representation, differential motion, dynamic analysis and control. Trajectory planning, actuators, sensors and low-level robotic vision. Artificial Intelligence. Practical project involving the design of a robotic system.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 3709 or ECE 309; and ECE 3709L or ECE 309L.

courses.title: Communication Systems
courses.description: Introduction to communication systems: Continuous wave modulation and demodulation. Power efficiency, bandwidth efficiency and system complexity of modulation systems. Performance of Communication systems in noise. Sampling process and various types of pulse modulation, introduction to digital modulation and demodulation, optimal reception in Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN), bit error rate (BER) and symbol error rate (SER) evaluation.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3715 or ECE 315.

courses.title: Communication Systems Laboratory
courses.description: To study and implement the basic theory of the design and analysis of communications systems. To learn the operation of laboratory instruments used in modern communications systems.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major. Pre or Corequisite(s): ECE 4705 or ECE 405.

courses.title: Digital Signal Processing
courses.description: The analysis, design and implementation of finite impulse response, infinite impulse response, and adaptive digital filters. Introduction to digital signal processing algorithms including multirate signal processing, frequency domain analysis, and spectral estimation.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3101 or ECE 306.

courses.title: Digital Communication Systems
courses.description: Introduction to digital communication systems including baseband transmission systems, optimum receivers, digital modulation/demodulation and synchronization, channel equalization, orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), and error correcting codes.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 4705 or ECE 405.

courses.title: Machine Learning
courses.description: An introduction to machine learning and pattern recognition algorithms and their applications. Topics include supervised learning techniques, unsupervised techniques, and learning theory.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major and ECE 3715 .

courses.title: Advanced Control Systems
courses.description: Design of Feedback Control Systems using frequency domain and fuzzy logic. Practical project involving the design of a feedback control system.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3709 or ECE 309; and ECE 3709L or ECE 309L.

courses.title: Biomedical Signals, Instrumentation and Measurements
courses.description: Fundamentals of biomedical signals, measurement and instrumentation; biomedical transducers; membrane biophysics, electrophysiology of excitable cells, membrane models; theory of bioelectrical signal detection, electrocardiography, electromyography; bio-potential electrodes, amplifiers and instrumentation techniques, Electrical safety in medical environment.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3101 or ECE 306.

courses.title: Power Transmission Lines
courses.description: Advanced methods of analysis of power systems, per-unit system, single-line representation of power systems, transmission line design and operation. Use of power systems analysis software for the solution of system problems, and introduction to power flow.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3810 or ECE 310.

courses.title: Power Transmission Lines Laboratory
courses.description: Experiments and computer modeling using available software to simulate the characteristics of power transmission systems under various operating conditions. Corequisite(s): ECE 4821 .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; ECE 3810 or ECE 310.

courses.title: Power System Analysis
courses.description: Power system stability and fault conditions, specific design considerations, symmetrical and unsymmetrical faults, symmetrical components, system protection, and economic operating practices. Use of computer software for fault and stability analysis.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3810 or ECE 310.

courses.title: Power System Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: Experiments and computer modeling to demonstrate fault conditions, instability, and protection methodology in power systems. Corequisite(s): ECE 4822 .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3810 or ECE 310.

courses.title: Power Systems Electronics
courses.description: Power electronic applications for industry and power utilities. The emphasis is on the analysis and design of power system components- including single and three-phase DC rectifiers, controlled rectifiers, and DC to AC converters. Selected applications include HV-DC transmission, resonant converters, AC and DC motor drives, static var control, and power quality issues.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 2200 , ECE 220, or ECE 299.

courses.title: Power Electronics
courses.description: Basic principles of Power Electronics with an emphasis on the analysis and design of DC switch-mode power supplies and DC to AC inverters using pulse-width modulation (pwm). Design of basic circuit topologies, control modes (voltage /current, etc.), control stability, high power factor design, pwm amplifiers, selection of magnetic components and output filters.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 2200 , ECE 220, or ECE 299.

courses.title: Wind and Solar Power Systems
courses.description: Wind resource characteristics, aerodynamic and electrical properties of wind power conversion systems, fixed speed and variable speed wind turbines, fundamental wind turbine modeling, basic operation principles of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, PV array design and installation, interconnection of solar PV and wind turbines to power grids.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 3810 or ECE 310.

courses.title: Illumination Engineering
courses.description: An introduction to light as waves and particles, photometric units, color, vision, luminairs and controls. Basic lighting measurements and calculations. Selected sections of State and Federal regulations and requirements.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 2101 , ECE 209, PHY 1520 or PHY 122.

courses.title: Introduction to Illumination Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: This lab is a demo tool and a practical platform for lighting experimentation. Experiments comprise of light sources and systems, photometric and electrical analysis and the practical use of photometric and electrical analytic equipment. Lab experiments verify various physical laws, cover outside measurements, photometry of sources and luminaries, and practical analysis and design of indoor lighting systems. Detailed individual and team reports are required; industrial manufacturing and utilities’ lab visits are included and required. Corequisite(s): ECE 4890 .
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 2101 , ECE 209, PHY 1520 or PHY 122; and ECE 4890 .

courses.title: Special Study for Graduate Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at graduate level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major and graduate standing.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Numerical Modeling
courses.description: Numerical techniques for solving engineering problems. Topics covered include Solutions of Equations of One Variable, Spline Interpolation, Numerical Integration, Numerical Linear and Algebra concepts like Gaussian Elimination, Pivoting, Matrix Factorizations, Special Matrices: Positive Definite Matrices, Orthogonal Matrices, Norms of vectors and matrices, Conditional Numbers, Eigenvalues, Singular Value Decomposition or generalized eigenvalues for singular or non-square matrices.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major and graduate standing.

courses.title: Matrix Methods
courses.description: Application of matrix methods in engineering analysis and also matrix concepts. Topics include matrix algebra and concepts, special matrices. Ranks of matrices, Eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Generalized inverses, quadratic forms, and engineering and mathematical applications in image processing, analysis of structures, circuit analysis, statistics, numerical analysis, data mining.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, undergraduate course in linear algebra, and graduate standing; OR consent of instructor.

courses.title: Performance and Reliability Analysis
courses.description: General concepts and advance techniques to conduct performance and reliability assessment for systems. Theoretical background and design mechanisms will be discussed. Modeling and simulation techniques and tools will be applied.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, upper division courses in probability and programming, and graduate standing.

courses.title: Network Security
courses.description: General concepts on network security including cryptography, cryptoanalysis, ciphers, keys, encryption, and hashing. Standards, mathematical backgrounds, programming implementations will be covered. Development tools and analysis tools will be used. Also, security concepts and practices in many other fields and respects such as hacking, Google security, Ajax security, cloud security.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major and graduate standing.

courses.title: Embedded Systems
courses.description: The theoretical and practical essentials of embedded systems including real time systems. Topics include the hard core concepts of real time systems like fault tolerance, and real time scheduling; exemplary microcontrollers such as H3A/C12, PIC with coverage on the architecture, hardware interface and interrupts, software with C coding, implementation, testing and debugging; and PDA such as IPhone, Android etc. with coverage on the basics, models, interfaces, and programming. Also, internet of things.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and ECE 3301 or ECE 341.

courses.title: Nanoelectronics
courses.description: This graduate course introduces engineering and applied science students to the science of miniaturized nanoelectronics; including fabrication of small machines (micro and nano size), characterization of materials, scaling laws, nanowire, carbon nanotube, grapheme, and nanosensor application. May be taken unlimited times.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and ECE 3250 or ECE 302.

courses.title: Systems Theory
courses.description: Application of matrix theory and linear vector spaces to the mathematical representation of systems. Analysis of the state equations for linear, time varying and invariant, continuous and discrete systems, controllability and observability for linear systems. Full state and reduced observers.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, ECE 3709 or ECE 309, and MAT 2240 or MAT 224.

courses.title: Random Processes
courses.description: Analysis of random phenomena associated with communications, signal processing, and computer engineering applications. Investigation of random binary signals, thermal noise, and Markov processes in communications, data mining, and machine learning. Applications include optimal filtering, estimation theory, Kalman filtering, online filtering, social networking, and queuing theory
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; graduate standing; and ECE 3715 , ECE 315, or upper-division undergraduate course in probability.

courses.title: Communication Theory
courses.description: Selected advanced topics in communication systems such as information theory for continuous and digital signals and systems; digital modulation techniques, optimum receivers for additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels and error rate performance, carrier phase estimation and time synchronization methods, digital communication through band-limited channels, and adaptive equalization. 3 hours lectures/problem-solving.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and ECE 4705 or ECE 405.

courses.title: Robust Control
courses.description: Advanced frequency domain techniques for systems with plant parameter uncertainty and external disturbances. Quantitative Feedback Theory. H2 and H design methods.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; graduate standing; and ECE 3709 , ECE 309, or upper-division course in control system.

courses.title: Advanced Software Engineering
courses.description: Object-Oriented and Classical Software engineering processes including requirements engineering, specification techniques, design concepts and methods, software testing and integration concepts, verification and validation, quality assurance, configuration management, Multimedia Software Design, Application modeling using Unified Modeling Language.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and ECE 3310 or ECE 304.

courses.title: Digital Image Processing
courses.description: Basic concepts in digital image processing such as image sampling and quantization, color, point operations, linear image filtering, correlation, image transforms. Image processing applications such as image restoration, image segmentation, image compression, and pattern recognition.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, ECE 3101 or ECE 306, and ECE 3715 or ECE 315.

courses.title: Solid State Devices
courses.description: Theory, modeling and applications of devices used in modern integrated circuits. Band structures carrier scattering and recombination processes and their influence on transport properties. Working principle of pn diode, BJT, MOSFET, GaAs and optical devices.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and ECE 3200 or ECE 320.

courses.title: Digital Signal Processing
courses.description: Analysis and design of signal modeling and its applications. Linear prediction filter, Wiener filter design and implementation using FIR and lattice filters. Non-parametric, parametric and Eigen system algorithms for power spectrum estimation.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and upper-division course in digital signal processing.

courses.title: Wavelet Theory and Applications
courses.description: Basic concepts in wavelet theory such as filters, down sampling and up sampling, filter banks, orthogonal filter banks, biorthogonal filter banks, multi-resolution analysis, wavelets, M-channel filter banks, integer wavelets, and applications.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and upper-division course in digital signal processing.

courses.title: Computer Arithmetic
courses.description: Redundant number systems, Fast Adders, Tree and array multipliers, Division by convergence, Floating point operation, Functional evaluation, High throughput, Low-Power and Reconfigurable arithmetic.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and ECE 4300 or equivalent..

courses.title: Computer Network
courses.description: Basic Principles and Protocols of TCP / IP (Transmission Control Protocol and Internet Protocol) Suite. Local Area Network (LAN). Analyze, simulate, and develop TCP / IP programs. Network tools. Design of engineering network. Also, related IEEE 802.11 Wireless standards.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and ECE 4303 or equivalent.

courses.title: Information Theory and Coding
courses.description: Introduction to source coding theorem, channel coding theorem, encoder and decoder design of linear block codes, Reed-Solomon codes, convolutional codes, turbo codes, and low density parity check codes.
courses.prerequisites: ECE major, graduate standing, and upper-division course in probability and random variables.

courses.title: Advanced Microprocessors
courses.description: State of the art 32-bit microprocessors; assembly language programming; input/output techniques; system design and peripheral interfacing. 4 hours lectures/problem-solving.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; graduate standing; and ECE 4320 and ECE 4320L , ECE 343 and ECE 343L, or ECE 432 and ECE 432L.

courses.title: Radar Signal Processing
courses.description: Introduction to radar systems including monostatic, bistatic and multi-static radar systems. Fundamental systems design concept and resolution limitations. Selected advanced topics of signal processing in radar systems, synthetic aperture radar system, adaptive radar clutter suppression, and super-resolution algorithms.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, ECE 4705 or ECE 405, and ECE 4708 or ECE 408; OR instructor consent.

courses.title: OFDM and CDMA Systems
courses.description: Fundamentals of Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) and Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) as they apply to current 4G, and 3G networks, respectively. Current trends in the wireless industry regarding multi-carrier systems. Receiver design in OFDM systems. Channel estimation and mitigation of other distortions, e.g., frequency offsets.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and ECE 4705 or ECE 405.

courses.title: Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Grammatical structure and parsing of natural language, rule based and statistical model (using corpus) of processing, representations of meanings (semantics), story understanding and generation, text characterizations, information retrieval, applications.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, ECE 3310 or ECE 304, and ECE 3715 or ECE 315.

courses.title: Introduction to Robotics, Haptics, Control and Applications
courses.description: Introduction to the science and engineering of manipulation and haptics. Kinematics, dynamics, statics, trajectory planning and control of robot manipulators. Basic principles of robotics will be learned through a study of common industrial robot systems analysis and design. Basic research on the wide range of applications of robotics is presented. Hands-on project involving telerobotics and haptic systems.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, ECE 3709 , MAT 2240 , and MATLAB programming.

courses.title: Smart Grid in Power System
courses.description: Study of Smart Grid in Power System Network, in particular study of power generation, transmission, distribution, storage, renewable and green energy. Description of components of a power grid system, their interactions and effects on the grid system. Information fusion and system integration. Decision support tools, smart metering, and study of available computer tools in the market.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, ECE major, and ECE 3810 or ECE 310.

courses.title: Distribution System and Power Quality
courses.description: Characteristics of power distribution system, analysis of voltage drop, power loss, and voltage regulation, design of power lines and substations, system planning, automation and protection, power quality phenomena, analysis and mitigation of voltage sag and variation, overcurrent, frequency oscillations, and harmonics in distribution network.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and ECE 3810 or ECE 310.

courses.title: Electric Vehicle and Energy Storage
courses.description: Electric vehicle (EV) technologies, EV motor design and control, vehicle dynamics, EV interaction with electric power grid, energy storage technologies and applications, energy storage estimation for solar PV and wind power systems.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, and ECE 3810 or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Digital System Testing
courses.description: Basic theories and techniques for testing digital systems. Test generation for combinational and sequential logic circuits, Fault Modeling, Fault Simulation, Testing for stuck faults, Automatic Test Generation, Design for Testability (DFT), Built-In-Self-Test (BIST) and Diagnosis, Boundary Scan and Core-Based Testing.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and ECE 3300 or equivalent.

courses.title: Design and Analysis of Computer Algorithms
courses.description: Complexity analysis, recursion and recurrences, searching and sorting algorithms, file compression and cryptology, computational geometry, graph algorithms, linear and dynamic programming, parallel algorithms using systolic, wave front and perfect shuffles, Lower bound theory and NP-complete problems.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and ECE 3310 or ECE 304.

courses.title: Computer Organization
courses.description: Memory subsystems; Cache, main memory and virtual memories. Instruction pipelines and pipeline hazards, dynamic scheduling algorithms, instruction level parallelism. Multiple instruction issues, multi-core processing.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; and ECE 4300 , ECE 425, or upper-division undergraduate course in computer architecture.

courses.title: Microcontroller Applications Laboratory
courses.description: Design and implementation of some microcontroller applications. Experiments will include implementation, testing, writing report of microcontroller hardware application. Design and testing of individual final student projects..
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and ECE 3301 or ECE 341.

courses.title: Digital Signal Processing (DSP) Applications Laboratory
courses.description: Design and implementation of DSP algorithms. Experiments will include digital filter design, adaptive filter design, modulator/demodulator design, and power spectral estimation.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and upper division course in digital signal processing.

courses.title: Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) Design Laboratory
courses.description: Modeling digital hardware using Verilog HDL, Implementation of digital hardware using FPGA.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major and graduate standing.

courses.title: Research Methods
courses.description: Introduction to research methods with emphasis on proposing, planning and documenting an engineering masters thesis or project; critical assessment of published research; and the writing, publication and presentation of technical articles.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major and graduate standing.

courses.title: Wireless Communication Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Conduct experiments in a variety of currently relevant, prevailing Wireless Digital Communications aspects and techniques, including: Propagation loss and link budget analysis, OFDM LSE channel estimation, MIMO System Simulation, Non linearity effects to 2G Cellular, the importance of constant envelope modulation, OFDM STBC with Alamouti codes, Multiple Receiving Antenna QAM modulated OFDM.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, graduate standing, and ECE 4705 or ECE 405.

courses.title: Advanced Communication Systems
courses.description: Selected topics in advanced communication systems such as multichannel and multicarrier digital communications, fading and multipath countermeasures (equalization, diversity, channel coding), spread spectrum, basic multiuser MIMO communication systems, and current topics in communication.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major; and ECE 5440 or ECE 544.

courses.title: Advanced Signal Processing
courses.description: Selected topics in adaptive signal processing applications in temporal and spatial domain. Least mean square algorithm, recursive least square algorithm, fast adaptive filter and non linear adaptive filtering.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Major, Graduate Standing, and upper division course in digital signal processing.

courses.title: Advanced Computer Organization
courses.description: Multicore processors, scalable shared memory multiprocessor systems, communication and synchronization, shared memory and data storage, systems on a chip. Current research topics related to multiprocessors.
courses.prerequisites: ECE Majors only; and ECE 5850 or ECE 585.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research in a specialized area, under the direction of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Independent Research
courses.description: Individual study/investigation and research in a specialized area proposed by the student with the approval, and under the supervision, of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Project
courses.description: Continued work on a Master’s Degree Project after a student has completed the required ECE 6910. Presentation of project in acceptable written and oral form. Individual and independent work based on the project proposal, plan and schedule approved by advisor. Regular meetings and discussions with advisor. Credit assigned upon acceptance of the project.
courses.prerequisites: ECE 6910 , advancement to candidacy, good academic standing; graduate standing, and completion of approved project proposal.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Thesis
courses.description: Individual study program under supervision of master’s thesis advisor. Presentation of thesis in acceptable written and oral form. Credit assigned upon completion of the thesis. A total of 6 units are required. Can be taken over two semesters (3 units + 3 units) or over three semesters (2 units + 2 units + 2 units)

courses.title: Master’s Degree Continuation
courses.description: Enrollment in this course allows candidates that have enrolled in the maximum number of thesis or project units to maintain resident status in order to receive university services.
